description: Blended-payment (principal plus interest) mortgage payments where the quoted annual rate is compounded half-yearly or yearly, not in advance.

citations.title: Interest Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. I-15), section 6 (Act current to 2026-10-29)
citations.used_for: Blended-payment mortgages must state the rate 'calculated yearly or half-yearly, not in advance'. This is why the checker supports exactly two compounding bases: semi-annual and annual.

citations.title: FCAC, Credit agreement for a fixed interest loan for a fixed amount (Mortgage), information box example
citations.used_for: Shows the standard disclosure wording for a fixed-rate mortgage: 'This interest is compounded twice per year but charged monthly.' Basis for semi-annual as the default. Its $4,565.87 payment includes a property tax portion that is not broken out, so it is NOT used as a numeric test case.

formula.periodic_rate: i = (1 + j/m)^(m/k) - 1, j = quoted annual rate as a decimal, m = compounding periods per year, k = payments per year
formula.payment: PMT = P * i / (1 - (1 + i)^(-n)), n = amortization_years * k; if j = 0 then PMT = P / n
formula.balance_after: B_t = P*(1+i)^t - PMT_rounded * ((1+i)^t - 1)/i, using the payment rounded to the cent, as a lender would charge it
formula.total_interest: PMT_raw * n - P (unrounded payment, so the figure does not depend on how the final payment is adjusted)

rounding: Payment, balance and total interest are rounded to the cent, half up.
grading_note: Payment must match to the cent. Balance and total interest get plus or minus $1.00 because lenders differ in how they round per-period interest; that spread is a few cents to well under a dollar over a 5 to 30 year schedule.
